# DocumentedOperandType

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="native" /> <Badge type="info" text="off by default" /> <Badge type="info" text="PHP ≥ 8.0" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Report an arithmetic or bitwise operation on an array or an object when
PHPDoc says the operand cannot take part in it. The code may hold a number at
run time, since PHP does not check PHPDoc, but the operation and the
documentation disagree. Operands the code alone proves wrong are
InvalidOperandType's.

## Example

```php{5}
<?php
/** @param int[] $counts */
function bump($counts): int
{
    return $counts * 2;
}
```

Reported:

<ul>
<li>line 5: Use a number here, not int[].</li>
</ul>

## Detection

- An operand of `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `%`, `**`, `&`, `|`, `^`, `<<` or `>>`,
  or of the compound assignment of one of them.
- The types of both operands are the ones PHPDoc-aware inference gives:
  `@param`, `@var`, `@return` and `@property` tags count.
- Every member of the operand's type is an array, or every member of it
  is a class whose whole hierarchy is known.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Operands InvalidOperandType reports.
- `+` between arrays, which merges them: an array operand of `+` is
  reported only when the other operand is known and cannot be an array.
- An operand that may also be null, a scalar or an unresolved class.
- An object of a class that takes part in arithmetic: `GMP`,
  `BcMath\Number`, `FFI\CData`, `SimpleXMLElement` and their subclasses.

## Fix

None: either the operation or the documentation is wrong.

## PHP versions

Active from PHP 8.0, where these operations throw a `TypeError`.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "DocumentedOperandType": {
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore DocumentedOperandType
```
